text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.68% today as oil prices stabilized after several days of geopolitical turbulence. Over the past week, the stock climbed 11.5% alongside a sharp recovery in crude prices—Brent crude topped $106 just yesterday following a Saudi airport attack, and while prices have eased today as markets weigh competing supply risks (potential Russian diesel flooding global markets versus possible disruptions from Iran-U.S. tensions), they remain well above prior levels. As an oil producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when crude prices rise; the company's earnings improve with each dollar-per-barrel increase.

The recent volatility reflects genuine geopolitical uncertainty: escalating Iran-U.S. tensions, ongoing Saudi-Houthi conflict, and shifting U.S. policy toward Russian energy sanctions all create supply-side risk that keeps oil prices elevated. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, this uncertain but firmer price environment supports higher valuations than the company had a week ago.
